intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Mirrors experiment:nova: NuMI has had no beam since July 2024 ("The MI has not operated since July 2024", Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting).
intervals.quote: 13.6×10²⁰ POT from 555.3 s of integrated beam-pulse time recorded between February 6, 2014, to March 20, 2020

intervals.label: last reported: no NuMI beam
intervals.note: Last reported beam condition; restart is not confirmed in the Atlas source audit on 2026-11-19. The open end retains the last reported condition as an assumption, not a new observation that the shutdown persisted. The April 2026 PAC report says MI had not operated since July 2024; the Fall 2026 report (PDF pages 4-5) still describes stable beam on 1 October as planned and the restart as upcoming. The proposed NuMI run remains a separate planned interval. A later report of operation should close this interval; passing a scheduled date must not do so. Here shutdown means no NuMI beam data-taking, not that the detectors are powered down. Fermilab's July 2026 feature describes NOvA as taking data without identifying its type; that broader statement does not resolve the more specific beam-operation reports.
intervals.quote: The MI has not operated since July 2024

intervals.label: NuMI beam run (planned; detector beam-data schedule)
intervals.locator: Fall 2026 PAC report, PDF page 4, accelerator-complex findings (FY27 run and planned stable beam); April 2026 report, PDF page 3, stretch schedule
intervals.note: Derived beam-data schedule from the NuMI source plan, not an independent detector-operation or restart report. The Fall 2026 PAC report plans 12 weeks of FY27 operation, with a 20-week stretch goal. The February 2027 end retains the April report stretch schedule; it is not an observed end.
intervals.quote: stable beam is planned for October 1

total_mass.note: Conflict: NOvA PRD 106, 032004 describes the near detector as "290 ton"; the NOvA public page and the 2025 monopole paper say 300 t / 0.3 kt.
total_mass.quote: The 0.3 kt Near Detector is located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target and 100 m underground at Fermilab

summary.plain: A small copy of the NOvA far detector, about 300 tonnes, sitting underground at Fermilab a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is made. It measures the beam before the neutrinos have had time to change type.
summary.technical: Functionally identical 0.3 kt PVC-cell liquid-scintillator tracking calorimeter 1 km downstream of the NuMI target and 100 m underground at Fermilab, on the same 14.6 mrad off-axis line as the far detector.

technology.quote: Charged particle tracking is accomplished via PVC cells filled with a mineral oil-based liquid scintillator.
technology.value: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, functionally identical to the far detector
